newsitem.title: USA: FOCUS-Hebdo buy to boost CUC's on-line commerce.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Hebdo buy to boost CUC's on-line commerce.

text.p: CUC International Inc will extend its reach in global on-line commerce with a $440 million agreement to acquire Paris-based classified advertising publisher Hebdo Mag International.

CUC said Thursday it will issue about 17 million new shares for the purchase -- the exact number set by an average of CUC's share price preceding the deal's close, expected in October. CUC now has about 434 million shares outstanding.
Hebdo is owned by founders Louise and John MacBain and Canada's Torstar Corp, publisher of the Toronto Star.

Torstar said in a separate announcement that it has agreed to sell its 50 percent stake in Hebdo to CUC. The MacBains will sell their half and continue to manage the business on a day-to-day basis, according to CUC.

"This is a good strategic fit, as classified advertisements are integral to our goal of reaching consumers just before every significant purchasing decision they make," said Walter Forbes, CUC chairman and chief executive, in a prepared statement.

"Classified advertisements generate high-volume consumer traffic, which drives our ability to convert members to netMarket," he said, adding that in France, Hebdo already conducts more than 30 percent of its business interactively.
"We intend to take that model into our netMarket service," Forbes said in the statement.
netMarket is CUC's Internet commerce site, where membership costs $69 per year, a CUC spokeswoman said.
CUC shares were off 1/16 to 26-1/16 in afternoon NYSE trade, while shares of HFS Inc, which announced an $11 billion merger with CUC in May, where off 1/4 at 62-7/8.
At January 31, CUC said it had 350,000 interactive members, a level that has since grown to 375,000, she said.
When the HFS transaction was announced, CUC said its overall membership stood at about 68 million.
The Hedbo deal will add $5 million to $7 million to CUC's pre-tax earnings in the 1997 calendar year, the spokeswoman said.
Hebdo is expected to report 1997 revenues of $200 million and $60 million in earnings before income taxes, depreciation and amortization, CUC said.

In CUC's fiscal year ended January 31 1997, the Stamford, Conn., company posted income before income taxes and one-time charges of $456.2 million. Revenues for the period were $2.3 billion, net income was $164.1 million and per share earnings after one-time charges were $0.41 per share.

CUC is a membership-based consumer services company with offerings ranging from educational and entertainment software to a full-service travel agency to the Welcome Wagon service and Entertainment coupon books.
Hebdo was founded 10 year ago by the MacBains, who will continue to jointly manage the business.

Hebdo has operations in 12 countries, including Canada, France, Sweden, Hungary, United States, Italy, Russia, and the Netherlands. The company publishes over 150 titles in 12 countries on three continents.
CUC will gain access to Hungary, Russia and the Netherlands with the acquisition, the spokeswoman said.
